placements.why: Both segments describe an internal HR/operations procedure (new-hire onboarding via the Pallasine checklist) rather than client-facing strategy, product, or architecture content. No existing strata category covers organizational/internal-process material — Opportunity, Strategy, Product, Architecture, Proof, Templates, and Calibration are all oriented toward engagement delivery or methodology, not internal staffing operations. This is the first content in the repo that names an internal-org-process subject, so it establishes the Organization strata category the instructions anticipate growing one real mint at a time.
placements.title: Internal operational processes get tracked as their own governance layer
placements.frame: What internal process — staffing, onboarding, team structure — is this envelope reporting the current, ratified shape of?

placements.title: Onboarding becomes a codified, mandatory checklist that displaces informal documentation
placements.frame: What does each version or iteration of the onboarding checklist reveal about how the organization defines a complete, legitimate first week for a new hire?
placements.why: src-1 states the Pallasine checklist as a universal, unhedged mandate ('every new hire completes') naming its concrete components (accounts, pairing rotation, shadow shift) — this names a standing subject (the onboarding standard) that future onboarding-related envelopes will keep feeding, not a one-time fact. src-2 supplies the checklist's provenance ('replaced the old wiki page last quarter'), which per the grain test is a fact evidencing the same theme — the checklist's standing as the current legitimate onboarding process — rather than a leaf of its own; it is folded in as supporting evidence for why this checklist, not the old wiki, is now the answer to 'what constitutes onboarding.' The position pass's PallasineChecklistAuthority frame (description + provenance jointly establishing legitimacy) corroborates treating both segments as one theme rather than two.
